title: Welcome to the B2A Economy: How Agents Buy | Andreessen Horowitz
gist: Testing four consumer shopping agents (Muse, Grok Bot, Instinct, Dots) across 1,270 prompts and 11,307 runs plus YipitData agent-spend data, a16z finds agents pick from narrow shared shortlists, optimize fully loaded cost and trust over small discounts, differ by agent, favor aggregators/marketplaces, and fail on login-gated checkout—so brands must sell to agents (B2A) with machine-readable pages, transparent pricing, persona-specific value and agent-friendly checkout.

themes.theme: Narrow agent shortlists and default picks

insights.claim: In tests across Muse, Instinct, Grok Bot and Dots, a product picked by one shopping agent had a 73% chance of being picked by at least one other agent, and in nearly a quarter of cases all four agents chose the same top product.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Agent recommendations concentrate on shared defaults, creating winner-take-most dynamics for brands that become the agent default in a category.
insights.locator: 1. Lean into use cases where you “spike”

insights.claim: Meta's Muse agent almost always starts with a search of its own Meta catalog capped at 50 options, and when it also uses browser search it looks at only about three product pages on average, so agent shortlists are very narrow.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Being present in the agent owner's own catalog (e.g., Meta's) is a gating distribution asset; platforms that own catalogs control the shortlist.
insights.locator: So how do you become a default pick?

insights.claim: Agents currently choose from their small research set based mainly on a consistent set of variables, namely price and reviews; the authors expect this to change as agents gain real-time metadata access and can browse every product in a category.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Today price and review signals dominate agent selection; watch for agents gaining full-category browsing, which would erode incumbent default advantages.
insights.quote: it picks out of that set based on a pretty consistent set of variables – namely, price and reviews.
insights.locator: The amount of overlap in recommendations

insights.claim: Brands can flip an agent's default pick by proving superiority for narrower use cases or personas: agents chose the cheaper Shark FlexStyle over the Dyson Airwrap in 91% of generic comparisons, but Dyson won 51% for fine or color-treated hair and 88% for daily use.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Premium brands can defend against agent-driven price commoditization by surfacing persona-specific feature data (weight, temperature, sound) that justifies the premium.
insights.locator: As one example – agents asked to choose between two hairdryers

insights.claim: For general graphic design software requests, agents nominated Canva in 78% of runs and Adobe in none, but Adobe appeared much more often when team templates were mentioned and was chosen in every case when professional-level output was required.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Agent-driven discovery favors simple, cheap defaults (Canva) for broad queries; incumbents like Adobe must win via specialized, high-end positioning.
insights.locator: Agents follow similar logic in selecting software.

insights.claim: Shopping agents search differently from traditional LLMs: LLMs rely on training data plus review sites, press and forums to surface options, while agents first check stored user memory, then internal connectors and catalogs, then external web search, and are more likely to visit direct or third-party product pages.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: The SEO-for-agents playbook shifts weight from press/review placement toward structured, machine-readable product pages.
insights.locator: 2. Optimize your product page for agent crawlers

insights.claim: Per The Prompting Company's activity logs, Muse and Dots use proprietary search systems while Grok Bot and Instinct use Exa for web search.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Exa is an infrastructure beneficiary of agent commerce; search-provider choice determines which pages agents can find.
insights.locator: Muse and Dots both use proprietary systems for search

insights.claim: An agent needs to establish what a product does, what it costs and what limits apply before placing it in its final option set, making an agent-readable website or agent-accessible software product crucial.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Companies lacking clear machine-readable pricing and capability info risk exclusion from agent-mediated purchases.
insights.quote: An agent needs to establish what your product does, what it costs, and what limits apply to put it in the final option set.
insights.locator: While the mix of sources an agent checks varies

insights.claim: When asked to generate ads from a product photo, OpenAI's Dots agent rejected Midjourney because it has no general API and prohibits automated usage, and chose Ideogram because its product page linked to an API, an official MCP integration and code examples.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Software vendors without APIs/MCP or with anti-automation policies lose agent-driven demand; API-first tools gain a new acquisition channel.
insights.locator: We asked Dots to generate ten ads

insights.claim: Agents calculate the fully loaded cost of a product including shipping fees, subscription terms, return/refund policies and warranties, and when two retailers offered the same price, agents chose the retailer with the better return policy in 86% of tests.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Return policies, shipping and warranty terms become direct ranking factors for agent commerce; retailers should expose them prominently.
insights.quote: Unlike humans, agents are ruthless optimizers.
insights.locator: 3. Agents do the math

insights.claim: Quince ranks in the top 15 retailers by consumer agent spend despite not being a top-15 global retailer, because its product pages surface pricing, free shipping, stock status, reviews and direct price comparisons to traditional retail and specific brands.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: DTC brands with transparent, comparison-ready pages can punch above their weight in agent commerce, a potential share-shift away from legacy retail.
insights.locator: Quince is one example of a retailer

insights.claim: Porkbun ranks #9 in agent transactions and #1 in technology, beating Cloudflare (#17) and GoDaddy (#112) even though they register 2.6x and 4.8x more domains per month, because Muse and Dots favor its transparent pricing with no discounted year-one price that later jumps.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Teaser-pricing and lock-in business models (e.g., GoDaddy) are penalized by agents; transparent pricers gain share in agent-mediated purchasing.
insights.locator: Software products can benefit from pricing for agents too.

insights.claim: Across 275 real-store comparisons pitting a cheaper seller against a more expensive but more trusted one, agents recommended the trusted option 72% of the time, e.g., Grok Bot picked a $250 Sonos speaker from an authorized dealer over a $200 listing citing warranty coverage.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Trust signals—traffic, backlinks, brand—still matter in agent commerce, protecting authorized dealers and established brands from pure price competition.
insights.quote: This is where traffic, backlinks, and brand still matter.
insights.locator: There is, however, a breaking point

insights.claim: Agent price sensitivity has thresholds: discounts under 10% did not sway agents at all, 10–50% discounts led agents to choose a cheaper, less trusted option only 24% of the time, and discounts above 50% made agents steer clear as too good to be true.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Discount-led acquisition is largely ineffective with agents; deep discounts can actively hurt conversion.
insights.locator: On the price front, a discount less than 10%

themes.theme: Each agent is a different customer

insights.claim: Bot-blocking shapes agent behavior: in Amazon checkout tests Grok Bot reached the cart in all runs while Muse, Instinct and Dots were blocked in all attempts, and Grok Bot linked to Amazon in 17.5% of runs versus no more than 1.6% for any other agent.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Amazon's blocking of most agents diverts agent-driven demand to other retailers; watch whether Amazon's stance changes as agent commerce grows.
insights.locator: 4. Treat each agent like a different customer

insights.claim: Muse linked to Walmart in 26% of answers and Best Buy in 22%, and the authors expect agent retailer preferences to strengthen as agents strike deals, citing Muse and Walmart launching an agent-to-agent communication channel.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Agent-retailer partnerships (Meta–Walmart) may become a new form of paid shelf space, favoring retailers that sign deals early.
insights.quote: We expect these preferences to strengthen over time as agents ink deals with retailers.
insights.locator: These preferences can be strong.

insights.claim: ChatGPT recently removed a claim that OpenAI partnerships would not impact product recommendations, signaling agent recommendations may become commercially influenced.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Agent recommendations could evolve into a monetizable ad/partnership channel for OpenAI, analogous to search ads.
insights.locator: Muse and Walmart are launching an agent-to-agent communication channel

insights.claim: Agents weigh evidence differently: Muse cites reviews in just 10% of picks versus 30–41% for other agents, Dots cites professional product tests in 11.4% of runs versus at most 3.7% for others, and Instinct disputes given ratings, with better reviews winning only 4 of its 26 tiebreakers.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Merchants must tailor signals per agent (reviews, professional tests, return terms) rather than optimize for one generic agent.
insights.locator: Agents also trust different evidence.

insights.claim: Instinct is the agent most likely to send users to a brand's direct website rather than a larger retailer, and weighs returns or cancellation terms much more heavily than other agents.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: DTC brands may find Instinct a relatively favorable channel; generous return/cancellation terms help win it.
insights.locator: Of all four agents, Instinct was the most likely

insights.claim: Agents also differ in how they market a product: Grok Bot and Instinct both picked Granola for in-person meeting notes with similar reasons, but Instinct built a visual site of options while Grok Bot gave a plain answer and offered to take notes itself.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Agents can act as competitors to the software they recommend (offering to do the task themselves), a disintermediation risk for app vendors.
insights.locator: Another difference across agents worth considering

themes.theme: Aggregators, marketplaces and travel dominate agent spend

insights.claim: Nearly one-third of observed spend among the top 50 merchants by agent spend went to marketplaces and aggregators, rising to 46% including retailers with third-party marketplaces and 55% including conventional multi-brand retailers.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Agent commerce is reinforcing aggregator power; single-brand merchants must manage their presence on these platforms.
insights.locator: 5. Be where agents already search and transact

insights.claim: Travel is the largest share of agent spend so far: in YipitData's sample Expedia and Booking.com were the two largest merchants by spend, with American Airlines and United ranked #4 and #6.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Online travel agencies are early winners of agent commerce, countering the view that AI agents disintermediate OTAs.
insights.locator: This is at least somewhat skewed by the fact that travel

insights.claim: Agents favor aggregators because they put options, prices and booking tools in one place; in a test, a refundable hotel room cost $476.20 direct versus $476 on Expedia, which also offered pay-now or pay-at-property options, making Expedia the agent's clear choice unless the user asked for direct booking.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Hotels' direct-booking strategies are weakened under agent shopping unless they match aggregator price and payment flexibility.
insights.quote: Unless the user asks for direct booking, the agent’s choice is clear.
insights.locator: Aggregators are attractive to agents

themes.theme: Connectors, checkout and agent payments rails

insights.claim: External connector usage by agents is currently low: in runs between October 22 and November 8, Grok Bot offered to connect an app in 5% of runs and Instinct, Muse and Dots each in fewer than 1%; agents mostly rely on their own catalogs and browser use.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Connector/app-integration distribution is still nascent; catalogs and browser-readable pages matter more today.
insights.locator: Currently, agents primarily lean on their own product catalogs

insights.claim: Platforms are rapidly building agent commerce infrastructure: OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT lets verified businesses add product feeds and publish a Business Agent, Meta feeds its product catalog into Muse, and Shopify Catalog makes products purchasable with Shop Pay across Muse, Grok Bot and Instinct.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Shopify is positioned as a cross-agent commerce layer; product-feed ownership becomes a competitive moat for platforms.
insights.locator: However, this is changing quickly.

insights.claim: Agents reached the end of the checkout form in 81% of runs on stores offering guest checkout, but every run on stores requiring a logged-in account stopped early, sometimes switching to another merchant.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Mandatory account login is a direct conversion killer for agent traffic; merchants should enable guest checkout.
insights.locator: Once an agent finds and picks your product

insights.claim: Stripe's Link wallet is used by Muse, Grok Bot and Instinct; for Muse it enables instant checkout at more than a million businesses and issues single-use virtual cards elsewhere, with user approval in chat without sharing card details.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Stripe is emerging as a key payments rail for agent commerce across multiple agents.
insights.locator: In the long term, identity-less shopping is not ideal

insights.claim: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet for Dots on November 13, initially for U.S. Pro users, letting the agent pay through existing checkout flows with a token instead of actual card details and user approval per purchase.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: OpenAI is vertically integrating into payments, potentially competing with Stripe/Shop Pay as an agent wallet.
insights.locator: After our tests ended, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet

insights.claim: a16z sees a big opportunity for startups that help businesses understand how to market and sell to agents (a B2A economy), as almost every business will want to tap agents as a new distribution channel.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore, Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Signals a16z investment appetite in agent-commerce optimization tooling (e.g., firms like The Prompting Company).
insights.quote: We see a big opportunity for startups helping businesses understand how to market and sell to agents.
insights.locator: We see a big opportunity for startups
